_about: Track reference (State Blob White Paper V1, layer 6). One entry per F1 25 track id. Sector-level location needs nothing from here (the sector start distances come off the wire in the Session packet). Corner-level location is used ONLY when 'calibrated' is true: run tests/calibrate_track.py over a real capture of the track, copy the fitted dist_m values in, review them against a lap you know, then set calibrated to true. Until then the corners list is names only and the booth says 'through the final sector', never 'into turn six'. 'character' and 'overtaking_spots' are plain-language facts the writer may use as colour; every capitalised word in them is licensed when they are offered. V8 (09 OCT): a track may also be 'estimated': corner distances laid out from the published layout, not fitted. Then corner names are used with a wider window (the booth may say 'into the chicane' from race one) until calibrate_track.py replaces them and calibrated is set true.

5.name: Monaco
5.character: Monaco is the tightest street circuit on the calendar: barriers on every metre, almost no straight, and only one real place to pass, so qualifying sets the race, the pit stop is the main way to gain a place, and one touch of the wall ends the day
overtaking_spots: the Nouvelle Chicane, out of the tunnel
Sainte Devote, with a good exit from Antony Noghes

5._distances_note: Monaco (Circuit de Monaco), F1 25 track id 5, post-2015 19-turn layout, 3337 m. published_dist_m: median of the F1 live-timing corner markers (via MultiViewer/FastF1, archived by TracingInsights) over ten sessions, 2024 and 2025 Monaco GP (FP1-3, qualifying, race); per-corner spread 16-33 m; scaled x1.0136 from the telemetry lap length (3292 m) to the official 3337 m. ref_apex_m: where the speed minimum sits on Norris's 2025 pole lap, same scaling; given only where one clean minimum sits within 60 m of the marker. calibrate_track.py matches the game's speed minima to these and moves dist_m. Names and notes: Mike's Item 10 dossier (28 OCT 26), checked against the timing data. Two changes from it: its distances ran 100-200 m short from turn two to turn sixteen, so the timing medians are used; and La Rascasse is turn eighteen (the slow right at 2899 m, about 65 km/h), not turn seventeen, which is the unnamed left kink before it. Directions (left/right) taken from the x/y trace. Unnamed turns are spelled out. Not yet calibrated: no F1 25 Monaco capture.

14.name: Abu Dhabi
14.character: Yas Marina is a power circuit: the North Hairpin opens onto a back straight of over a kilometre into the chicane, then a second straight into the banked Marsa Corner, and the lap finishes in the slow, twisting hotel section, so the passing comes at the chicane and Marsa Corner and the lap is lost or won under the hotel
overtaking_spots: the chicane at the end of the back straight
Marsa Corner at the end of the second straight
turn one, with a good exit from the final corner under the hotel
14.drs_zones_note: DRS zone one: the back straight from the North Hairpin to the chicane. DRS zone two: the second straight from turn eight to Marsa Corner.

14._distances_note: Abu Dhabi (Yas Marina), F1 25 track id 14, 2021-onward 16-turn layout, 5281 m. published_dist_m: median of the F1 live-timing corner markers (via MultiViewer/FastF1, archived by TracingInsights) over ten sessions, 2024 and 2025 Abu Dhabi GP (FP1-3, qualifying, race); per-corner spread 18-42 m; scaled x1.0099 from the telemetry lap length (5229 m) to the official 5281 m. ref_apex_m: where the speed minimum sits on Verstappen's 2025 pole lap (1:22.207), same scaling. calibrate_track.py matches the game's speed minima to these and moves dist_m by the difference. Check against the wire: real sector 2 starts at 1210 m and sector 3 at 3567 m (pole lap, timing split vs distance); the F1 25 Session packet says 1211 m and 3538 m. The North Hairpin and Marsa Corner both sit just after a sector line. Directions (left/right) taken from the x/y trace of the same lap. Names: authentic only; unnamed turns are spelled out.

17.name: Austria
17.character: the Red Bull Ring is short and fast, three big braking zones on the climbs and a quick run back down, so the field stays close and a small mistake costs a place
overtaking_spots: turn three at the top of the hill
